title: GPM, LPM, m³/h: The Pump-Curve Trio
h1: Pump flow units — GPM, LPM and m³/h
description: 1 US gpm = 3.785 L/min = 0.2271 m³/h. Pump curves from US, EU and IEC vendors all use different units on the same graph.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Same pump curve, three flow axes. Pick the wrong one and best-efficiency-point drifts by 20%.
body: Centrifugal pump curves come with the flow axis in whatever the manufacturer's home country prefers. Selecting a pump means matching duty flow — and unit — precisely, or you land off the BEP and destroy efficiency.

> 1 US gpm = 3.7854 L/min = 0.22712 m³/h = 0.06309 L/s
> 1 UK gpm = 4.546 L/min = 0.27277 m³/h (20% larger than US gpm)
> 1 m³/h = 4.403 US gpm = 3.666 UK gpm = 16.67 L/min

US gpm: North American water, HVAC, fire pumps. UK gpm: UK water utilities, occasional legacy specs. L/min and L/s: European water and HVAC. m³/h: process industry, chemical, EU pump vendors. bbl/day: oil production.

A chiller specced 200 US gpm = 45.4 m³/h = 757 L/min. A European pump vendor's 45 m³/h pump is right on duty. A pump specced '200 gpm' from a UK vendor is 20% higher than intended — wildly oversized, throttling wastes 30% power.
US and UK gallons differ by 20%. Convert to m³/h or L/min once, compare.

faqs.q: Is US gpm the same as fluid-ounce-based gpm?
faqs.a: US gpm uses 128 fl oz per gallon by the US gallon (231 in³). Do not use UK fl oz to derive it.
bbl/day for production, gpm or L/min for surface pumps. Convert with 1 bbl = 42 US gal.
